about.title: Turlock Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Turlock trust the providers they see in Stanislaus County, and most of the time that trust is well placed. Medicine is hard, and a poor result is not automatically negligence. A malpractice claim comes down to a narrower question: did a doctor, nurse, hospital, or clinic fall below the standard of care a reasonably careful provider would have met, and did that lapse cause real harm? Answering that almost always takes a qualified medical expert, not just a patient's instinct that something felt off. California's MICRA rules add their own layer. The clock generally runs one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day notice must go to the provider before a suit is filed. Non-economic damages are capped, though the cap rises each year. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Turlock residents with an independent attorney who can review records, consult the right expert, and explain honestly whether a case exists.

whyChoose.title: Why Turlock Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines that start earlier than you think
items.desc: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from discovering the harm and no more than three years from the injury, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement. An attorney can pin down which date controls in your situation before options close.

items.title: Expert review, not guesswork
items.desc: California courts nearly always require a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. The attorneys in our network know how to obtain records and line up that opinion.

items.title: Honest talk about what a case is worth
items.desc: MICRA caps non-economic damages at an amount that rises every year, while economic losses like medical bills and lost wages are treated separately. You'll hear how those rules apply to you, without anyone promising a result.

items.question: I was treated in Turlock but transferred to a larger hospital outside Stanislaus County. Where does my claim belong?
items.answer: Malpractice claims can involve more than one provider across more than one location, and the care you received at each stop matters. An attorney will gather records from every facility and sort out which providers, if any, fell short and where a claim should be filed. You don't need to figure that out on your own before reaching out.

items.question: My outcome was bad, but does that mean I have a malpractice case?
items.answer: Not by itself. California law separates unfortunate results from negligent ones, and only the latter supports a claim. A qualified medical expert has to compare what was done against what a careful provider would have done in the same circumstances. That review is exactly what an independent attorney arranges.

items.question: What does it cost to have a Turlock attorney look at my situation?
items.answer: Using LawProactive costs nothing, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. If an attorney concludes there isn't a viable claim, you'll be told plainly and owe nothing.
